report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **true**. Research consistently shows that receiving bystander hands-only (compression-only) CPR is associated with significantly higher survival rates after an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest compared to receiving no bystander CPR.

### Evidence Summary
* **Substantial Survival Benefit:** Immediately initiating CPR can double or triple a patient's chances of surviving an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest compared to no CPR intervention.
* **Improved Clinical Outcomes:** Observational and registry studies demonstrate that both compression-only CPR and conventional CPR lead to significantly higher overall survival and favorable clinical outcomes compared to receiving no bystander assistance.
* **Reduced Time to Action:** Hands-only CPR reduces friction for untrained laypersons, enabling faster initiation of chest compressions and maintaining crucial continuous blood flow until emergency responders arrive.

### Sources
* **American Heart Association CPR & First Aid:** https://cpr.heart.org/en/resources/cpr-facts-and-stats
* **MDedge:** https://www.mdedge.com/ehospitalistnews/article/18117/trauma/compression-only-cpr-increased-cardiac-arrest-survival
* **Scientific Reports (Nature):** https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-022-27096-9?error=cookies_not_supported&code=c4f5f5e4-21e8-48cb-b407-c90f12e714ba
* **Medical Xpress:** https://medicalxpress.com/news/2019-04-compression-only-cpr-survival-out-of-hospital-cardiac.html
